content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a shrinkage loss and mixup regularization to improve the interpolation ability of I2I model.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
pros:

1.  the paper is well-written and it is important to address the smooth interpolation problem of I2I.

cons:

Very important baselines are missing.  

1. The paper focus on interpolation of I2I but ignore literature [1]. In fact, the shrinkage loss is very close to one of the proposed regularizations in [1]. Specifically, to regularize the latent style space to be small, this paper proposes ||s1-s2|| and [1] proposes ||s1||.

2. There are also some works using mixup in latent space, specifically, based on StarGAN-V2., e.g., see[2]



[1] Liu, Yahui, et al. "Smoothing the disentangled latent style space for unsupervised image-to-image translation." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2021.

[2] Cao, Jie, et al. "Remix: Towards image-to-image translation with limited data." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2021.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper designs a shrinkage regularizer and a latent mixup strategy to help the task of MMUIT. This two contributions make it able to generate samples that smoothly change between different domains. Ablation studies are also conducted to verify the effectiveness of each contribution.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The shrinkage loss compacts the latent space. According to the results of ablation study, it seems that such a loss is beneficial to generated diversity (reflected by FID), and is harmful to LPIPS. 
2. The mixup strategy is intuitive, but indeed brings up evident performance gain.
3. The proposed metric $P^2$ is hoped to facilitate the relevant research.

Weakness:
1. Please check the Eq. (4), I can't understand this formulation. Maybe there are some mistakes.
2. To my knowledge, StyleGan is also able to translate between two images with different attributes. What's the differences or advantages of the MMUIT methods equipped with the proposed shrink loss and mixup strategy comparing with StyleGan?
3. The references and comparison methods are almost before year 2020. You should provide more comparisons with recent state-of-the-art methods.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The proposed shrinkage loss is novel in the field of MMUIT. The written of this paper can be further improved. E.g, you could provide an algorithm flow in training, which will make the reader to understand it easily.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed regularizers and the designed $P^2$ metric is useful for MMUIT. In summary, this is a nice work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes two tricks to smooth the latent space for I2I translations and one metric for evaluation. The paper is well-written. The tricks and the metric are achieved by slightly changing the existing methods, thus the novelty is limited.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- The paper is well-written. The proposed tricks are proved to be effective for the I2I tasks.

Weaknesses:

- The proposed shrinkage loss is similar to the uniform loss as mentioned in the paper. The proposed mixup strategy is used similarly to the earlier work, but just the authors applied it to the feature space instead of the pixel space. I doubt the novelty of the two tricks. 

- Moreover, what if the authors directly apply the uniform loss and the mixup strategy in the pixel space? Will they perform worse than the proposed tricks? The authors should really compare with the potential baselines, instead of only comparing with basic I2I work such as Stargan v2.

- I’m curious about the trade-off between diversity and smoothness in the latent space, especially since the authors use an L2 regularization for paired style features. There exists some work [1] for evaluating diversity (precision and recall) for generative models. The authors didn’t analyze this enough in the paper.

- How are the style distributions, F(z) and E(x), different from each other?

[1] T. Kynkäänniemi, et al., Improved Precision and Recall Metric for Assessing Generative Models, NeurIPS 2019.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The contributions are clear and supported by the results. The novelty is limited. The paper attached the code in the supplementary material.
content.summary_of_the_review: Due to the weaknesses mentioned above, I believe this work is not qualified to be accepted.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper discusses that existing image translation methods usually perform poorly when interpolating between different domains due to insufficient inter-domain data. To address this, the authors suggest new regularization methods that guide a model to have a compact and smooth latent space and provide a new metric that measures the degree of interpolation smoothness.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros
The paper is well-written and the idea is simple but effective. The proposed method seems to be generally applicable to other i2i models and present promising results.

Cons
The main motivation of the paper is that the desired characteristic of i2i models is to have a smooth change between different “domains”. This argument needs more backups. The novelty seems to be limited. The proposed method is a small variation of the existing methods. 

Questions

The main motivation of the paper needs more support: the desired characteristic of i2i models is to have a smooth change between “different domains”. Is that so? If that is the case, why? In what kind of practical application or situation should it have such characteristics? The authors just stated the argument without any justification (at least some practical examples one can think of) even though it is the core basis of the entire discussion. Let me play devil’s advocate here: 
Just because the existing method suffers from interpolation between domains is not sufficient to support the need for the method. It's easy to imagine the benefits of smooth intra-domain interpolation, but I'm not sure what the benefits of good inter-domain interpolation are. This might be too artificial setup. Why would a generator need to cover unrealistic (non-existing) inter-domain regions too? 

In equation (9), the discriminator has to discriminate the generated image with mixed styles. From its loss design, it seems like there is no solution, doesn’t it?; e.g., the half-cat and half-dog is not realistic anyway when compared to “real” data of dogs and cats. Wouldn’t this confuse the generator training? Where can a generator get an incentive on producing such intermediate creatures? If I understood correctly, this is entirely upon how the latent space is encoded while training, which seems too naïve. 

In addition, the authors argue that the bad performance of existing methods seems to come from the lack of data in the inter-domain regions. Wouldn’t this be actually the desired behavior of the model? (since there is no creature that is half cat and half dog and the goal of generators are to mimic the “real” data distribution)  

In addition, wouldn’t making the latent space compact (forcing the points to come closer) bad for having disentangled representations? 

Can one use P^2 as a regularization as well? (as PPL was in StyleGAN2)?

content.title: Smooth image-to-image translations with latent space interpolations
content.TL;DR: We are regularizing the latent spaces to have super smooth image-to-image translations. We also created a metric to quantitatively measure how smooth the translations.
content.abstract: Multi-domain image-to-image (I2I) translations can transform a source image according to the style of a target domain. One important, desired characteristic of these transformations, is their graduality, which corresponds to a smooth change between the source and the target image when their respective latent-space representations are linearly interpolated. However, state-of-the-art methods usually perform poorly when evaluated using inter-domain interpolations, often producing abrupt changes in the appearance or non-realistic intermediate images. In this paper, we argue that one of the main reasons behind this problem is the lack of sufficient inter-domain training data and we propose two different regularization methods to alleviate this issue: a new shrinkage loss, which compacts the latent space, and a Mixup data-augmentation strategy, which flattens the style representations between domains. We also propose a new metric to quantitatively evaluate the degree of the interpolation smoothness, an aspect which is not sufficiently covered by the existing I2I translation metrics. Using both our proposed metric and standard evaluation protocols, we show that our regularization techniques can improve the state-of-the-art multi-domain I2I translations by a large margin. Our code will be made publicly available upon the acceptance of this article.
